papers.title: Detecting Emotional Signals of Relationship Well-Being Using AI: A Cross-Sectional Comparison of Transformer-Based and Lexicon-Based Models for Couples Therapy Research.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Natural language processing and AI models are increasingly used to extract emotional signals from textual data; however, systematic validation of different computational paradigms in emotionally complex relational contexts remains limited. Such approaches may contribute to digital health research, particularly in the fields of digital mental health and couples therapy, where understanding emotional expressions within romantic relationships is especially relevant. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare a lexicon-based approach (NRC Emotion Lexicon) and a transformer-based model (Pysentimiento) in detecting affective patterns within spontaneous romantic relationship narratives and to evaluate their criterion-related associations with a theory-driven measure of relational well-being. METHODS: In this cross-sectional exploratory study, 112 Spanish adults completed the Couple Flourishing Measure (CFM) and provided an open-ended description of their romantic relationship. Narratives were analyzed using both computational approaches to generate emotion and sentiment indices. Pearson correlations were computed between model outputs and CFM scores. Steiger Z tests were conducted to compare dependent correlations across models. RESULTS: Both approaches showed significant associations with couple flourishing, although the transformer-based model yielded stronger correlations for several affective dimensions, particularly positive sentiment (r=0.66, 95% CI 0.54-0.76) and negative sentiment (r=-0.74, 95% CI -0.82 to -0.65). The lexicon-based approach showed smaller associations, primarily for negative emotions. Steiger Z tests identified significant between-model differences for disgust (P=.04), joy (P=.01), sadness (P=.004), surprise (P=.03), and positive and negative sentiment (both P<.001), but not for anger or fear. CONCLUSIONS: In this sample, Pysentimiento showed stronger associations with couple flourishing than the NRC Emotion Lexicon across several affect

papers.title: The predictive validity of the Ontario Domestic Assault Risk Assessment (ODARA) for men's intimate partner violence recidivism in fixed follow-ups of 1 to 5 years.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Intimate partner violence (IPV) recidivism risk assessment is a routine part of the police response to incidents involving assaults between marital, cohabiting, or dating partners. Reliance on such tools to inform critical decisions about risk management and victim safety requires ongoing research to ensure validity and utility for emerging practice issues, such as estimating risk over specific time periods. HYPOTHESES: We predicted that the Ontario Domestic Assault Risk Assessment (ODARA) would predict IPV recidivism in data from three police organizations, but with significant variability between sites. METHOD: We tested the ODARA's predictive validity among 567 men charged for IPV against a female partner during an average 6-year follow-up and fixed follow-up periods of 3 months to 5 years at risk. RESULTS: The ODARA total score (raw M = 5.80, SD = 2.52; prorated M = 6.00, SD = 2.64) as scored by researchers (ICC = .944) significantly predicted postindex charges for IPV recidivism (n = 157, 27.7%) in the overall follow-up (Harrell's C = .62) and in 6-month to 5-year fixed follow-ups with small to medium effects ranging from AUC = .63-.69. At 3 months, IPV recidivism was 3%, and AUC was small (.61) and nonsignificant. By 3 years, 74% of observed recidivism had occurred, with over 100 recidivist events. Data were combined with comparable rates from Hegel et al. (2022) and Olver and Jung (2017) to tabulate new 3-year IPV recidivism estimates from 977 men across four Canadian provinces. CONCLUSIONS: Low observed recidivism within 1 year prohibits interpretation of risk for more imminent violence, but 3-year fixed follow-ups are a reasonable standard for IPV recidivism research. The new recidivism estimates for the likelihood of IPV charges within 3 years can be used to interpret ODARA scores. Future research should replicate results in additional populations and develop standard risk levels for IPV. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserv

papers.title: Evolution from Platysma Myectomy to Myotomy: Preserving Lower Lip Function in Facial Synkinesis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Platysma hypertonicity, a sequela of facial synkinesis (FS), is treated with platysma myectomy. However, its close relationship to the facial nerve's cervical branch raises concern for postoperative lower lip dysfunction. This study compares lower lip outcomes following platysma myectomy, platysma myotomy at the thyroid cartilage level, and no platysma intervention. METHODS: Included were FS patients who underwent selective neurectomies and ipsilateral depressor anguli oris myectomy (NDAO) between 2019 and 2025. Mean follow-up was 12 months. Patient groups included NDAO (n=27), NDAO with platysma myectomy (n=19), and NDAO with platysma myotomy (n=10). Pre and postoperative commissure position, lower lip height, lower lip inclination angle, and lower quadrant dental show were measured using Emotrics and ImageJ. RESULTS: Patients were on average 52 years old. The NDAO group improved significantly across all outcomes (p ≤ 0.004); the myotomy group improved in inclination and dental show (p ≤ 0.014); the myectomy group showed no significant improvement. The myotomy group outperformed the myectomy group across all measures (p ≤ 0.006) and had better commissure position and dental show than the NDAO group (p ≤ 0.045). The NDAO group had significantly better lower lip height, inclination, and dental show than the myectomy group (p ≤ 0.018). CONCLUSIONS: Selective neurectomies with DAO myectomy alone and with platysma myotomy were associated with improved lower lip outcomes. Platysma myectomy was associated with postoperative lower lip elevation, consistent with possible cervical branch injury. Both platysmal approaches target cervical symptoms while the platysma myotomy also preserves lower lip position.

papers.title: Implementation of artificial intelligence-enabled, obstetric point-of-care ultrasounds into routine antenatal care in Lusaka Province of Zambia.
papers.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Access to obstetric ultrasound remains limited in many countries owing to the limited availability of equipment and specialist operators. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled obstetric point-of-care ultrasound (OB POCUS) may expand access to reliable gestational age (GA) dating within routine antenatal care (ANC). OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and clinical utility of implementing AI-enabled OB POCUS for GA assessment across four public-sector facilities in Lusaka Province, Zambia. METHODS: We integrated routine AI-enabled OB POCUS into ANC using a training-of-trainers model, followed by standardized competency-based training for facility healthcare providers and ongoing mentorship. We abstracted data from facility ANC registers for women scanned between September 2024 and March 2025. Among patients with both last menstrual period (LMP)- and AI-enabled OB POCUS-based dating, we calculated the discrepancy between the two estimates and applied American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) GA-specific thresholds to classify each patient according to whether the discrepancy was large enough to warrant revising the LMP-based estimated due date (EDD) to the AI-enabled OB POCUS-based EDD. We estimated the proportion meeting these re-dating criteria and used logistic regression to assess factors associated with meeting them. RESULTS: Among 1068 ultrasound recipients, 859 (80.4%) had both a recorded LMP and a documented AI-enabled OB POCUS-based EDD. Of these, the median EDD discrepancy was 11 days (IQR = 5-29 days), and 51% met the ACOG criteria for EDD revision. The proportion meeting re-dating criteria did not differ by GA at presentation and was not affected by facility or demographic characteristics. CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of AI-enabled OB POCUS within public-sector ANC in Zambia was feasible. papers.title: Maintaining Dynamic Crosslink Engagement Under Network Perturbation Limits the Loss of Hydrogel Viscoelastic Function.
papers.abstract: Dynamic hydrogels are widely used to emulate viscoelastic extracellular matrices, yet stabilization against dissolution does not necessarily preserve viscoelastic function under physiological swelling. Here, we interrogate how network topology governs the retention of dynamic mechanics in swollen hydrogels. Using a modular thiol-ene platform in which a dynamic supramolecular guest-host network is architecturally decoupled from the stable covalent network, we first demonstrate that as-prepared hydrogels occupy a structured, low-dimensional viscoelastic manifold parameterized by the relative fraction of stable and dynamic crosslinks. This structured design space demonstrates that hybrid network viscoelasticity can be rationally defined by the crosslinker composition across a broad range of relaxation behaviors. However, upon equilibration in aqueous media, this tunable viscoelastic space collapses; hydrogels spanning a broad range of relaxation extents converge toward a restricted mechanical regime despite preservation of the macroscopic structure, consistent with swelling-induced dilution of guest-host bonding partners that were never architecturally coupled to the stable scaffold. To restore dynamic function without increasing permanent crosslink density, we introduce multivalent electrostatic interactions to enforce heteropolymer proximity. Increasing crosslinker charge preserves frequency-dependent elasticity and dissipation in the swollen state, with the maximally charged crosslinker retaining a normalized high-frequency modulus approximately three-fold greater than that of the uncharged control. Competitive disruption confirms that viscoelastic retention remains contingent on guest-host engagement. Together, these findings reveal that limiting loss of viscoelastic function under swelling requires architectural coupling of reversible motifs to a stable network and that stabilization against dissolution alone is insufficient to preserve dynamic mechanical function

papers.title: Dynamic Electronic Structure of the FeMoco Enables Mechanistic Coupling between N2 Binding and H2 Evolution in Nitrogenase.
papers.abstract: The mechanistic coupling of N2 binding and H2 evolution through reductive elimination from the E4 intermediate constitutes a critical step in the nitrogenase catalytic cycle. Despite extensive mechanistic investigations, how the Fe centers within the FeMoco cofactor dynamically reorganize their local electronic structures to facilitate this coupled process remains unresolved. Here, using density functional theory (DFT) combined with intrinsic atomic orbital/intrinsic bond orbital (IAO/IBO) and natural bond orbital (NBO) analyses, we uncover the electronic structure evolution of FeMoco along the coupled N2-binding/H2-evolution reaction coordinate. Comparative analyses of reaction energetics, with appropriate transition states, support an "intermediate" mechanism over purely "associative" or "dissociative" pathways, revealing a key intermediate E4(H2N2) in which N2 and H2 are simultaneously coordinated to the same Fe center. Detailed molecular-orbital analyses demonstrate that the coupled reaction is enabled by highly synchronized electronic reorganization across neighboring Fe centers, which dynamically redistribute electron density to stabilize concurrent H2 release and N2 activation. In particular, cooperative Fe-Fe electronic coupling allows the reactive Fe site to adapt its local bonding interactions. These findings provide an electronic-level rationale for the functional necessity of the multinuclear FeMoco architecture and reveal how orchestrated electronic flexibility within the cluster governs the critical mechanistic step of nitrogenase catalysis.

papers.title: Formation of Antiferromagnetic Spin Dimer Induced by Orientation Ordering of Water Molecule in Fluorinated Pincered Cu(II) Complexes.
papers.abstract: Pincered transition metal complexes show rich crystal structures owing to intra- and intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Their structural diversity also motivates us to investigate their magnetic interactions mediated by hydrogen bonding. In this study, we report the structural and magnetic properties of copper mononuclear complexes 2FH-CuCl2·H2O and 3F-CuCl2·H2O, with a fluorinated pincered ligand. Both compounds are composed of a uniform chain of molecules coupled by O-H···Cl classical and improper hydrogen-bonding interactions. These compounds exhibit a structural transition induced by orientation ordering of water molecules, which drives bond alternation. The bond alternation also induces dimerization in magnetic interactions between nearest-neighbor Cu ions, evidenced by the magnetization following the isolated antiferromagnetic spin dimer model.

papers.title: Unlocking the ideal ohmic contacts in MoSi2N4via MSene electrodes.
papers.abstract: The pursuit of low-resistance ohmic contacts in two-dimensional semiconductor devices remains a critical challenge for practical applications. Here, using first-principles calculations, we investigate the interfacial contact properties between monolayer MoSi2N4 and three MSene electrodes (M2S, M = V, Mo, W). After identifying the most stable stacking configuration, we find a systematic Schottky-to-Ohmic transition from V2S to W2S, driven by increasing interfacial charge transfer from the semiconductor to the metal. Notably, W2S/MoSi2N4 forms an ideal n-type ohmic contact with zero Schottky barrier. Moreover, all three heterostructures exhibit vanishing tunneling barriers, attributable to covalent-like quasi-bonding interactions at the short interlayer spacings. Although conventional barrier engineering via interlayer compression is precluded by the already near-covalent distances, external electric fields can still modulate the Schottky barrier, albeit with reduced efficiency. Our results establish W2S as a promising electrode candidate for MoSi2N4-based devices and provide insights into dipole engineering for contact optimization in strongly coupled van der Waals heterostructures.

papers.title: Mating Market Shaped by Collective Religious Rituals.
papers.abstract: Collective religious rituals provide public settings in which individuals demonstrate commitment and gain social visibility. Research has largely focused on their role in social cohesion, while their relationship with marriage formation remains less well understood. Drawing on detailed participation history data collected in a Tibetan village in western China, we examine how participation in the annual June-Gathering, a major collective ritual festival among Amdo Tibetans, is associated with age at first marriage and the geographic origin of spouses. We distinguish three male-performed costly bodily rituals-mouth-piercing, back-piercing, and forehead-cutting-from statue-carrying, a highly visible collective activity. Event-history models indicated that accumulated prior participation in statue-carrying was associated with earlier first marriage, whereas the findings for three bodily rituals were mixed. In a Bayesian ordinal logistic model, statue-carrying provided the clearest evidence of an association with more geographically distant marriage ties; estimates for the bodily rituals were positive but uncertain. Statue-carrying thus showed the most consistent associations across the two marriage outcomes. These ritual-specific patterns offer limited support for a uniform costly-signalling account and highlight the potential relevance of social visibility and marriage opportunities. However, the observational data cannot distinguish opportunity from signalling processes or establish causal relationships. The findings connect collective religious participation to realised marriage outcomes while underscoring the importance of distinguishing activities within a shared ritual setting.

papers.title: Exploring the Feasibility of the LEAD Trial: Online Dyadic Dementia Care Planning for Early Alzheimer's and Other Dementias.
papers.journal: The American journal of hospice & palliative care
papers.abstract: ObjectivesPeople with dementia often lose decisional capacity before death, underscoring the need for dementia-focused advance care planning (ACP) tools. In cooperation with our Community Advisory Board, we developed LEAD (Life-Planning in Early Alzheimer's and Other Dementias), a Web-based, self-guided, dementia-focused ACP intervention for care partners and persons with preclinical or mild dementia. This study evaluated the feasibility and initial efficacy of the LEAD intervention.MethodsCommunity-based dyads (N = 48) of one care recipient (person with or at risk for dementia) and one care partner completed the intervention and study surveys assessing decision-making self-efficacy, relationship quality, and medical advance directive completion. We utilized mixed-effects repeated measures models to explore changes in outcome variables over time in care recipients and care partners.ResultsSixty-four percent of dyads completed the intervention. There was a significant increase in decision-making self-efficacy scores among care recipients and care partners (P < .001) and a decrease in relationship strain among care partners (P < .05). There were no changes in positive relationship domains. Of the 23 dyads that did not have a completed medical advance directive prior to the study, 13 dyads (50.0%) completed this document during the intervention.DiscussionOur findings suggest the LEAD intervention is feasible and demonstrates initial efficacy in promoting dementia-focused ACP. The LEAD intervention has the potential to reduce relationship strain and help care partners improve their confidence as proxy decision-makers for people with dementia who cannot make independent medical decisions.

papers.title: Peptides for male sexual dysfunction: a systematic review of emerging evidence.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sexual dysfunction remains highly prevalent among men and significantly impacts quality of life. Peptides are short chains of amino acids designed to mimic endogenous signaling molecules and modulate a variety of physiological pathways. AIM: To systematically review the available human evidence evaluating the effects of peptide and peptide-derived therapies on male sexual function, reproductive hormones, and semen parameters. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, crossover studies, prospective clinical studies, and experimental physiological studies evaluating peptide-based interventions in adult men. OUTCOMES: Outcomes of interest included erectile function, sexual desire, orgasmic and ejaculatory outcomes, reproductive hormones, semen parameters, and adverse events. RESULTS: Twelve studies comprising 372 male participants met inclusion criteria. Investigated peptides included melanocortin receptor agonists (PT-141/bremelanotide and Melanotan II), kisspeptin analogues, and oxytocin. Melanocortin receptor agonists demonstrated the most consistent improvements in erectile function, producing significant increases in penile rigidity and erectile duration in healthy men and men with erectile dysfunction, including sildenafil non-responders. Kisspeptin increased gonadotropin secretion, enhanced sexual brain processing, and improved penile tumescence and measures of sexual desire in men with hypoactive sexual desire disorder. Oxytocin showed mixed effects, with potential benefits on orgasm intensity, sexual satisfaction, and partner interaction, but no consistent improvements in erectile function, ejaculation latency, or semen parameters. papers.title: Predicting official recidivism among perpetrators of intimate partner violence against women: A random forest model.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Predicting recidivism in intimate partner violence against women (IPVAW) remains a major challenge in forensic and clinical practice. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a random forest model to predict official recidivism among men convicted of IPVAW, and to examine whether performance-based neuropsychological indicators contributed to prediction alongside psychosocial and criminogenic variables. HYPOTHESES: We expected the model to show moderate discriminatory capacity. We also hypothesized that executive functioning and attentional indicators would emerge as relevant predictors of official recidivism, together with substance misuse, childhood maltreatment, prior IPVAW behaviors, and social support. METHOD: The sample comprised 284 adult men court-mandated to attend a community-based intervention program. Official recidivism was defined as any new IPVAW incident and/or breach of judicial conditions during the 12-month follow-up after program completion. Baseline predictors included age, childhood maltreatment, social support, substance misuse, self-reported IPVAW behaviors, and neuropsychological performance. The random forest pipeline was evaluated using repeated nested cross-validation, comprising 10 outer folds repeated 10 times. Feature selection was conducted within each training fold using Boruta, followed by permutation-based importance filtering. RESULTS: The final model retained age, Variability and Commissions from the Conners' Continuous Performance Test-Third Edition, and Conceptual Level Responses, Perseverative Errors, and Perseverative Responses from the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test. Performance was modest (AUC = .65; accuracy = .70; balanced accuracy = .61; sensitivity = .46; specificity = .76; Cohen's κ = .19), with better classification of nonrecidivists; no psychosocial or criminogenic self-report variables were retained. papers.title: Association Between Painful Symptomatology and Domestic Violence During the Pregnancy of Adolescents and Young Adults: Results From the AMOR Project.
papers.abstract: Domestic violence (DV) is a public health issue with serious consequences for women's physical and mental health. During pregnancy, it increases the risk of anxiety and depression and worsens quality of life. Additionally, the physiological changes during this period lead to postural adaptations that contribute to lower back and pelvic pain. These impacts can be even more intense in pregnant adolescents, who are more vulnerable to pre- and postnatal complications, including premature births. The aim of this study was to assess the association between painful symptomatology and DV in pregnant adolescents and adults. This is a cross-sectional observational study resulting from the AMOR project (Adolescence and Motherhood Research), with 41 adolescents and 45 adults during the third trimester of pregnancy. DV (Hurt Insult Threatened Scream scale) and painful symptomatology (the Pelvic Pain Assessment Questionnaire of the International Society of Pelvic Pain) were assessed through self-report. Chi-square and Fisher's exact tests assessed the associations, considering p < .05. Violence perpetrated by a family member was reported by 33.7% of all the participants and was associated with pain when urinating (p = .035) and pain when sitting (p = .047). Intimate partner violence was reported by 23.3% of the sample and associated with pain during sexual intercourse (p = .041). Reporting violence from any source was associated with pain during sexual intercourse (p = .026) and pain when sitting (p = .047). When considering the sample stratified by age, violence perpetrated by family members was higher among adolescents (46.3%) than adults (22.2%; p = .018), and the associations between the different types of DV and painful symptomatology remained significant only among adolescents. papers.title: Intimate partner violence and its association with mental disorders among women in the general population, pregnant women and postpartum women: systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major global health and human rights issue. However, the association between IPV and specific mental disorders across different life stages, including pregnancy and postpartum, remains insufficiently quantified. AIMS: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess the associations between IPV and mental disorders among women in the general population, pregnant women and postpartum women. METHOD: We searched six databases to identify cross-sectional, case-control and cohort studies published between 1 January 1980 and 13 June 2024. A random-effects meta-analysis model was performed to derive the pooled odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: Of 7326 records identified, 82 studies with a total of 140 286 participants were included. For women in the general population, lifetime IPV was significantly associated with depression (odds ratio 2.26, 95% CI 1.83-2.79, p < 0.0001; class 1; moderate). Past-year IPV also demonstrated significant associations with depression (odds ratio 2.36, 95% CI 1.61-3.45, p < 0.0001; class 3; very low) and anxiety (odds ratio 2.85, 95% CI 1.61-5.05, p = 0.0003; class 3; low) among women in the general population. IPV during pregnancy was notably associated with depression (odds ratio 3.59, 95% CI 2.48-5.20, p < 0.0001; class 2; very low) and anxiety (odds ratio 3.27, 95% CI 2.60-4.10, p < 0.0001; class 1; moderate) in pregnant women. For postpartum women, lifetime IPV exposure was significantly linked to depression (odds ratio 2.09, 95% CI 1.54-2.83, p < 0.0001; class 3; moderate). CONCLUSIONS: IPV is associated with depression, anxiety and eating disorders among women in the general population, pregnant women and postpartum women. Tackling the root causes of IPV and improving access to mental health services are critical steps in mitigating the long-term psychological burden on women worldwide.

papers.title: The social roots of student mental health: Organizational opportunity structures, social capital, and loneliness.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Individual and clinical approaches to student mental health can obscure the role of universities as social environments. Within a social-capital framework, we examine whether loneliness links peer integration and student-faculty relationship quality to later psychological distress. METHODS: Three waves of the German National Educational Panel Study (NEPS SC5; N = 3014 enrolled students) linked relationship measures (2012) to loneliness (2013/2014) and psychological distress measured with the CDC Healthy Days instrument (2016). Indirect associations were estimated using OLS-based mediation models with 5000 bootstrap resamples, controlling for gender and age. Organizational opportunity structures are theorized but not measured. RESULTS: Higher peer integration and student-faculty relationship quality were associated with lower loneliness. Peer integration was associated with lower distress directly (B = -0.40, p < .01) and indirectly through loneliness (B = -0.22, 95% CI [-0.29, -0.15]); the indirect association represented 35.3% of the total association. Student-faculty relationship quality had no significant total or direct association with distress but showed a significant indirect association through loneliness (B = -0.15, 95% CI [-0.22, -0.08]). CONCLUSIONS: The findings are consistent with loneliness as a pathway connecting social relationships to later psychological distress. The faculty measure is considered in light of linking social capital, while the items primarily describe perceived relationship quality. Organizational opportunities for social connection provide a theoretical extension that requires direct testing.
